structure: Independent people drawn from a trivariate Gaussian population. The population moments satisfy records C and A; the two correlations involving Z are explicit scenario assumptions. No realized-sample standardization or moment matching is performed.

parameter_provenance.basis: Exact population means in X, Y, Z order.
Correlation times the two unit standard deviations.
Chosen missing relationship; also correlation_XZ because both variances are one.
Chosen missing relationship; also correlation_YZ because both variances are one.
Convenient joint shape, not required for the stated Pearson and OLS population formulas.

requested_estimands.name: partial_xy_given_z
requested_estimands.basis: For separate population OLS adjustments including intercepts, residual correlation is (0.5 - 0.6*0.5)/sqrt((1 - 0.6^2)*(1 - 0.5^2)). Records do not determine either correlation involving Z.

requested_estimands.name: marginal_xy
requested_estimands.basis: Directly fixed by record A, independently of Gaussian shape or the chosen Z relationships.

requested_estimands.name: slope_x_on_z
requested_estimands.basis: The population OLS slope with intercept is Cov(X,Z)/Var(Z). Record C fixes the denominator at one but supplies no X-Z covariance.

limitations: The adjusted correlation and X-on-Z slope are point scenarios, not consequences of the evidence alone. For example, setting both Z correlations to zero also satisfies the records but gives adjusted correlation 0.5 and slope zero.
Gaussian shape is assumed; the identified marginal correlation and the scenario's residual-correlation formula depend only on second moments.
Finite random samples will not exactly reproduce the stipulated population moments or estimands.
These artificial records support no clinical or causal interpretation.
